name: Question 5
problem: Let $F(x,y,z)=2z\,i+3x\,j-4y\,k$ and let $C$ be a path in ${R}^{3}.$ Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r?$
worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)\,i+Q(x,y,z)\,j+R(x,y,z)\,k
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x+Q(x,y,z)\,\text{d}y+R(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z.
$$

Therefore, in our case, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}2z\,\text{d}x+3x\,\text{d}y-4y\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Let F(x,y,z)=2zi+3xj−4yk and let C be a path in R3. Which of the following is equivalent to ∫CF⋅dr?

a
∫C2zdx+3xdy−4ydz
b
∫C−4ydx+2zdy+3xdz
c
∫C(2z+3x−4y)dxdydz
d
∫C3xdx−4ydy+2zdz
e
∫C2dx+3dy−4dz
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a piecewise-smooth path C and a vector field F(x,y,z)=P(x,y,z)i+Q(x,y,z)j+R(x,y,z)k defined on C, we have

∫CF⋅dr=∫CP(x,y,z)dx+Q(x,y,z)dy+R(x,y,z)dz.

Therefore, in our case, we obtain ∫CF⋅dr=∫C2zdx+3xdy−4ydz.
